rule: Built from the frozen questions, frozen top-5 snapshot and corpus only - before any Experiment C generation.

questions.question: What share of global anthropogenic methane emissions comes from agriculture?

units.text: Agriculture is the largest source of anthropogenic methane emissions
units.locate: largest source of (global )?(anthropogenic|biogenic) methane|biggest single contributor to anthropogenic methane

units.text: It accounts for about 42% of the global total (GMSR: almost 42 per cent in 2020)
units.dependency: 3 chunks: 2 GMSR + 1 UN SG restating GMSR -> 1 independent origin

units.text: 146 Mt per year (2020)

questions.evidence_boundary: Supports agriculture ~42% (2020) of anthropogenic methane. One GMSR chunk says 'biogenic' for the same figure; the UN SG chunk gives 42% without a year. All repeats trace to GMSR 2025: one origin, not corroboration.

questions.question: How many alerts did the Methane Alert and Response System send, and how often do operators respond?

units.text: MARS had sent over 5,000 alerts by February 2026 (cumulative)
Global response rate was 12% in 2025 (up from 1% in 2024)
Response rates grew nearly tenfold since the end of 2024

questions.evidence_boundary: 5,000 is cumulative to February 2026, not a 2025 figure. 12% is a global response rate for 2025, not a share of all alerts. No per-operator or per-country rates beyond 'only 11 countries above 70%'.

questions.question: What are the main challenges in modernising electricity grids?

units.text: Demand growth outpaces grid expansion: connection queues, competition for scarce capacity, service disruption
Stability / system strength as converter-connected resources displace synchronous generators
Distributed resources and two-way flows create voltage, transformer loading, feeder and protection challenges

questions.evidence_boundary: Challenges are qualitative in the top-5; no quantified costs (e.g. congestion costs, 330 GW) are retrieved.

questions.question: How can the cost of capital for clean energy projects in emerging and developing economies be reduced?

units.text: At least a tripling of international concessional funds (USD 90-110 billion a year) to improve risk-return
units.origin: IEA Reducing the Cost of Capital

units.text: Better risk management: strong policy frameworks and regulation, and de-risking instruments
units.origin: IEA Reducing the Cost of Capital

units.text: Address sector-specific risks (different business models, project scales, prevalent risks)
units.origin: IEA Reducing the Cost of Capital

units.text: A 1 percentage point reduction saves about USD 150 billion a year (impact, not a 'how')
units.origin: IEA Reducing the Cost of Capital

questions.evidence_boundary: Top-5 supports the 'how' (concessional funds, policy/regulation, de-risking, sector-specific risks) and the size of the benefit. It does not give country-specific measures.

questions.question: How are near-zero emissions steel and cement defined?

units.text: Steel: 400-50 kg CO2-eq per tonne of crude steel, depending on scrap share
Cement: 125-40 kg CO2-eq per tonne of cement, depending on clinker ratio

questions.evidence_boundary: Supports the IEA-derived near-zero thresholds and that they slide with scrap share / clinker ratio.

questions.question: What role does concessional finance play in cutting methane emissions and in clean energy investment in developing economies?

units.text: Clean energy: at least a tripling of international concessional funds (USD 90-110 bn/yr) to improve risk-return and mobilise private capital
units.locate: tripling in international concessional funds|tripling of concessional funding
units.origin: IEA Reducing the Cost of Capital

units.text: Methane: grants and highly concessional donor funding should scale up and coordinate to fill gaps
Emerging economies seek technology transfer and concessional finance to bridge capacity gaps
units.locate: seek technology transfer and concessional finance

questions.evidence_boundary: Two separate literatures: IEA (clean energy, quantified) and UNEP/UN (methane, qualitative). No single figure for methane-specific concessional finance is retrieved.

questions.question: How fast is electricity demand expected to grow in Europe, India and Indonesia, and how much must grid capacity expand globally by 2035?

units.text: Europe: electricity demand +80% or more, 2022-2050
India: more than 2.5 times
Indonesia: 3 times
Global grid capacity must increase by at least 30% by 2035 (25 million km of lines)

questions.evidence_boundary: Demand figures are 2022-2050 (Seasonal Variability); grid figure is to 2035 (Modernising Grids): different reports and horizons, which should not be merged into one timeline.

questions.question: What are the nine priority actions in the UN Secretary-General's call to action on methane?

units.text: Action 1: Fix leaks and eliminate routine flaring and cold venting
Action 2: Make methane measurable, reportable and verifiable
Action 3: Science-based global methane standard / near-zero-methane marketplace
Action 4: Produce food more efficiently with less methane
Action 5: Halve per-capita food waste and reduce food loss
Action 6: Reform incentives and redirect finance and subsidies
Action 7: Phase out open dumping and uncontrolled landfills
Action 8: Capture methane from waste and wastewater
Action 9: Build circular, low-methane urban waste systems

questions.expected_behaviour: answer the supported part and state the gap
questions.evidence_boundary: Top-5 contains only Actions 1, 5 and 6 (+ general text). Six actions are in the corpus but not retrieved.

questions.question: What are the near-zero emissions thresholds for steel and for aluminium?

Aluminium near-zero threshold

questions.expected_behaviour: answer the supported part and state the gap
questions.evidence_boundary: Steel supported; another retrieved proposal gives 380-400 kg CO2-eq/t hot-rolled steel by 2045 (different proposal and metric). Nothing on aluminium anywhere in the corpus.

questions.question: What would methane mitigation in the fossil fuel industry cost each year, and how does that compare with the sector's income?

units.text: About USD 98 billion a year (accounting for the value of recovered gas)
units.dependency: 3 chunks: GMSR + 2 UN SG chunks restating GMSR (footnote [23]) -> 1 independent origin

units.text: Equal to 2-4% of the sector's USD 2.4 trillion net income in 2023
units.locate: 2.4 per cent|two to four per cent|2–4 per cent

units.text: IEA's lower estimate: about USD 52 billion a year for a 75% reduction (~2% of net income)
units.dependency: restated in 2 UN SG chunks (footnote [24]) -> 1 origin, independent of GMSR

questions.evidence_boundary: Two different estimates with different scope (GMSR net cost of all measures; IEA cost of a 75% cut by 2030). Citing GMSR and the UN SG restatement of it is not independent corroboration.
